name: Concrete bag calculator
description: Slab volume translated into a whole-bag purchase quantity using the stated bag yield.
formula: L × W × D × (1 + waste) ÷ bag yield
variables: length (ft | m) = 10 | 3.048; width (ft | m) = 10 | 3.048; depth (in | mm) = 4 | 101.6; bagYield (ft³ / bag | ft³ / bag) = 0.6 | 0.6; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Bag yield is the user-entered value from the exact selected product label. | Waste is applied before whole-bag rounding. | This tool does not select mix strength or installation method.
sources: Sakrete: estimating bagged concrete jobs <https://www.sakrete.com/blog/post/estimating-bagged-concrete-jobs/>

name: Concrete column
description: Round concrete-column volume, ready-mix order and bag-equivalent estimate.
formula: π × (diameter ÷ 2)² × height × count ÷ 27 × (1 + waste)
variables: diameter (in | mm) = 12 | 304.8; columnHeight (in | mm) = 48 | 1219.2; count (count | count) = 1 | 1; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Each column is treated as a right circular cylinder. | All entered columns are treated as identical. | Ready-mix quantity is rounded to the next 0.25 yd³ after allowance.
sources: Concrete Network: volume calculation guidance <https://www.concretenetwork.com/concrete/howmuch/calculator.htm>

name: Concrete cost calculator
description: Preliminary material cost from a stated ready-mix quantity and local supplier rate.
formula: Ready-mix quantity × (1 + waste) × stated supplier rate
variables: volume (yd³ | m³) = 3 | 2.29366457395; unitPrice (USD / yd³ | USD / m³) = 185 | 241.970864573; waste (% | %) = 0 | 0
assumptions: Supplier rate is an editable planning input and may be stale. | Delivery, labor, equipment, tax and other costs are excluded. | Waste is applied only when the starting quantity excludes overage.
sources: Concrete Network: volume calculation guidance <https://www.concretenetwork.com/concrete/howmuch/calculator.htm>

name: Curb and gutter
description: Combined curb-and-gutter volume, ready-mix order and bag equivalent from run length and the two cross-section rectangles.
formula: V = length × (curb height × curb width + gutter width × gutter thickness) × (1 + waste) → ready-mix order
variables: length (ft | m) = 40 | 12.192; curbHeight (in | mm) = 6 | 152.4; curbWidth (in | mm) = 6 | 152.4; gutterWidth (in | mm) = 18 | 457.2; gutterDepth (in | mm) = 6 | 152.4; waste (% | %) = 8 | 8
assumptions: Section is two rectangles: curb head plus gutter pan. Battered faces are not modelled. | Ready-mix quantity is rounded to the next 0.25 yd³ after allowance. | This is not a civil detail, reinforcement schedule or city standard section.

name: Concrete driveway
description: Driveway volume, ready-mix order and bag-equivalent estimate with visible allowance.
formula: L × W × D × quantity ÷ 27 × (1 + waste) → ready-mix order
assumptions: Ready-mix quantity is rounded up to the next 0.25 yd³. | 40/50/60/80 lb bag yields are planning assumptions of 0.30, 0.375, 0.45 and 0.60 ft³; confirm the selected product label. | Truck-load equivalent assumes a 10 yd³ planning load, not supplier delivery capacity. | Waste is applied to net volume before purchase rounding.
sources: Concrete Network: volume calculation guidance <https://www.concretenetwork.com/concrete/howmuch/calculator.htm>

name: Concrete footing
description: Continuous footing volume, ready-mix quantity, and whole-bag equivalent.
formula: Footing length × width × depth × quantity ÷ 27 × (1 + waste)
variables: length (ft | m) = 20 | 6.096; width (ft | m) = 2 | 0.6096; depth (in | mm) = 8 | 203.2; quantity (count | count) = 1 | 1; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Footing geometry is treated as a continuous rectangle. | Ready-mix quantity is rounded to the next 0.25 yd³. | Bag and truck-load values are planning equivalents; confirm product yield and supplier delivery capacity. | Waste is applied before purchase rounding.

name: Concrete mix calculator
description: Volumetric cement, sand and aggregate split from a known wet volume using a stated mix ratio and dry-volume factor.
formula: dry volume = wet volume × dry factor; each material = dry volume × parts ÷ total parts
variables: volume (yd³ | m³) = 1 | 0.764554857984; cementParts (ratio | ratio) = 1 | 1; sandParts (ratio | ratio) = 2 | 2; aggregateParts (ratio | ratio) = 4 | 4; dryFactor (ratio | ratio) = 1.54 | 1.54; bagYield (ft³ / bag | ft³ / bag) = 1 | 1; waste (% | %) = 0 | 0
assumptions: Wet volume is converted to dry material volume with the entered dry-volume factor, a planning convention rather than a laboratory yield. | Parts describe volumetric batching only. They do not set compressive strength, slump or water-cement ratio. | Cement bags use the entered bag yield, commonly about 1.0 ft³ for a 94 lb US bag. | Sand and aggregate are dry volumes in the selected unit system, before supplier bulking and moisture adjustment.
sources: PCA: portland-cement bag yields and mix basics <https://www.cement.org/>

name: Concrete patio
description: Patio slab volume, ready-mix order and bag-equivalent estimate with visible allowance.
formula: L × W × D × quantity ÷ 27 × (1 + waste) → ready-mix order
assumptions: Ready-mix quantity is rounded up to the next 0.25 yd³. | 40/50/60/80 lb bag yields are planning assumptions of 0.30, 0.375, 0.45 and 0.60 ft³; confirm the selected product label. | Truck-load equivalent assumes a 10 yd³ planning load, not supplier delivery capacity. | Waste is applied to net volume before purchase rounding.
sources: Concrete Network: volume calculation guidance <https://www.concretenetwork.com/concrete/howmuch/calculator.htm>

name: Post hole calculator
description: Concrete volume and bag count for round fence or deck post holes, including solid sonotube piers when post diameter is zero.
formula: π ÷ 4 × (hole diameter² − post diameter²) × depth × count × (1 + waste)
variables: holeDiameter (in | mm) = 12 | 304.8; postDiameter (in | mm) = 4 | 101.6; depth (in | mm) = 36 | 914.4; count (count | count) = 10 | 10; bagYield (ft³ / bag | ft³ / bag) = 0.45 | 0.45; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Each hole is a right circular cylinder. Enter 0 post diameter to fill the hole or sonotube solid. | Post subtraction uses the entered post diameter only; it does not model flared bells or gravel bedding. | Ready-mix rounds up to the next 0.25 yd³ after allowance. | Bag yield must match the selected mix label. | This is a quantity estimate, not a footing or frost-depth design.
sources: Quikrete: post-setting and bagged-concrete calculators <https://www.quikrete.com/calculator/main.asp>

name: Slab rebar calculator
description: Preliminary slab rebar count, linear footage and bar-weight planning from spacing, cover and bar size.
formula: (floor(usable width ÷ long spacing) + 1) × usable length + (floor(usable length ÷ cross spacing) + 1) × usable width × (1 + waste)
variables: length (ft | m) = 20 | 6.096; width (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; longSpacing (in | mm) = 18 | 457.2; transSpacing (in | mm) = 18 | 457.2; edgeCover (in | mm) = 2 | 50.8; barSize (choice | choice) = 4 | 4; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: The slab is treated as a rectangular orthogonal grid with identical bar size in both directions. | Nominal unit weights are published CRSI designations: #3 = 0.376, #4 = 0.668, #5 = 1.043, #6 = 1.502 lb/ft. | Edge cover shortens each bar and is not a substitute for specified concrete cover to soil or weather. | Laps, hooks, chairs, dowels and temperature steel are not counted unless included in the allowance. | This is a planning quantity, not a reinforcement design.
sources: CRSI: reinforcing-bar weights and designations <https://www.crsi.org/>

name: Concrete slab
description: Volume, ready-mix order, and bag equivalent for a rectangle, circle, or L-shape.
formula: L × W × D × quantity ÷ 27 × (1 + waste) → ready-mix order
variables: shape (choice | choice) = 0 | 0; length (ft | m) = 20 | 6.096; width (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; diameter (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; notchLength (ft | m) = 8 | 2.4384; notchWidth (ft | m) = 6 | 1.8288; depth (in | mm) = 4 | 101.6; quantity (count | count) = 1 | 1; waste (% | %) = 8 | 8
assumptions: Ready-mix quantity is rounded up to the next 0.25 yd³. | 40/50/60/80 lb bag yields are planning assumptions of 0.30, 0.375, 0.45 and 0.60 ft³; confirm the selected product label. | Truck-load equivalent assumes a 10 yd³ planning load, not supplier delivery capacity. | Waste is applied to net volume before purchase rounding. | Circle uses diameter. L-shape subtracts the missing inner rectangle from the outer box.
sources: Concrete Network: volume calculation guidance <https://www.concretenetwork.com/concrete/howmuch/calculator.htm> | Sakrete: estimating bagged concrete jobs <https://www.sakrete.com/blog/post/estimating-bagged-concrete-jobs/> | ASTM C94/C94M: ready-mixed concrete <https://www.astm.org/standards/c94> | ACI: concrete floors and slabs <https://www.concrete.org/> | ICC IRC 2021 Chapter 5: floors (R506) <https://codes.iccsafe.org/content/IRC2021P2/chapter-5-floors>

name: Sonotube
description: Solid cardboard-tube volume, ready-mix order and bags. Post-hole annulus is a different tool when a post occupies the hole.
formula: π × (diameter ÷ 2)² × height × count ÷ 27 × (1 + waste) → ready-mix order
variables: diameter (in | mm) = 12 | 304.8; columnHeight (in | mm) = 48 | 1219.2; count (count | count) = 4 | 4; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Each tube is poured solid. The post is not subtracted — use post-hole when a post occupies the hole. | Ready-mix quantity is rounded to the next 0.25 yd³ after waste. | Diameter, depth and steel come from the approved design.

name: Concrete stairs
description: Triangular-step volume, ready-mix order and bag equivalent from riser, tread, width and count.
formula: V ≈ risers × width × tread × riser ÷ 2 × (1 + waste) → ready-mix order
variables: risers (count | count) = 10 | 10; riser (in | mm) = 7 | 177.8; tread (in | mm) = 11 | 279.4; width (ft | m) = 3.5 | 1.0668; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Each step is treated as a right-triangle prism: risers × width × tread × riser ÷ 2. | Closed risers, waist thickness, nosing and landings are not included. | Ready-mix quantity is rounded to the next 0.25 yd³ after allowance. | This tool does not size stringers, reinforcement or code geometry.

name: Concrete wall
description: Concrete wall volume with stated thickness, waste, and ready-mix rounding.
formula: Wall length × height × thickness ÷ 27 × (1 + waste)
variables: length (ft | m) = 20 | 6.096; height (ft | m) = 8 | 2.4384; thickness (in | mm) = 6 | 152.4; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: The wall is treated as straight, rectangular, and solid. | Openings and returns are not deducted in this quick takeoff. | Waste is applied before quarter-yard purchase rounding.

name: Concrete weight
description: Concrete tons from a stated volume and an editable density. Ready-mix yards stay the slab tool.
formula: tons = yd³ × density (lb/ft³) × 27 ÷ 2,000
assumptions: 150 lb/ft³ is a normalweight planning density. Lightweight and heavyweight mixes differ. | This is mass, not a ready-mix order and not a structural dead-load design. | Start from a volume you already calculated on a pour page.

name: Wire mesh
description: Welded-wire mesh sheet count from slab area and the face coverage of one sheet, with overlap sitting in the waste field.
formula: slab area × (1 + overlap) ÷ sheet coverage
variables: length (ft | m) = 20 | 6.096; width (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; sheetCoverage (ft² | m²) = 50 | 4.645152; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Overlap and cutting live in the waste field. A one-square lap on 5×10 sheets is close to 10% on a rectangle. | This is a sheet count, not a structural mesh design, chair layout or rebar substitute. | Roll products should use net coverage after the specified lap.

name: Drywall cost calculator
description: Preliminary drywall-sheet material cost from stated sheet quantity, rate and visible allowance.
formula: Base quantity × (1 + allowance) × stated material rate
variables: sheets (count | count) = 15 | 15; sheetRate (USD / sheet | USD / sheet) = 16 | 16; waste (% | %) = 0 | 0
assumptions: Material rate is an editable planning input and may be stale. | Any allowance remains visible before material pricing. | Labor, delivery, tax, accessories and installation are separate estimate components.

name: Drywall material calculator
description: Room drywall sheets, fasteners, compound and tape with visible opening deductions and purchase rounding.
formula: (wall area + optional ceiling − openings) ÷ sheet coverage × (1 + waste)
variables: length (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; width (ft | m) = 10 | 3.048; height (ft | m) = 8 | 2.4384; doors (count | count) = 1 | 1; windows (count | count) = 1 | 1; doorArea (ft² | m²) = 21 | 1.95096384; windowArea (ft² | m²) = 15 | 1.3935456; includeCeiling (choice | choice) = 1 | 1; sheetCoverage (ft² | m²) = 32 | 2.97289728; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Gross wall area uses 2 × (room length + room width) × ceiling height; ceiling is optional. | Door and window deductions are editable planning assumptions. | Companion-material estimates use 0.053 gal/ft² compound, 1.5 linear ft/ft² tape, 3.5 screws/ft² walls and 4 screws/ft² ceilings; confirm the selected system and installation method. | Waste is applied only to whole-sheet purchase quantity.
sources: CertainTeed: drywall materials estimate <https://www.certainteed.com/drywall-calculator> | CalcSummit: transparent drywall methodology <https://www.calcsummit.com/calculators/construction/drywall/>

name: Drywall compound
description: Ready-mix joint-compound gallons and 4.5 gal pail count from net board area using a 100 ft² per gallon taping-and-finish rule of thumb.
formula: gallons = ceil(area ÷ coverage per gallon × (1 + waste)); pails = ceil(gallons ÷ 4.5)
variables: coverage (ft² | m²) = 450 | 41.806368; coveragePerGallon (ft² / US gal | m² / US gal) = 100 | 9.290304; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: 100 ft² per gallon is a taping-plus-finish planning figure, not a one-coat label rate. | Pails round up at 4.5 gallons, a common ready-mix bucket. | Tape, beads, primer and texture are excluded.

name: Drywall fasteners
description: Screw count and 1,000-count box round-up from sheet count.
formula: screws = ceil(sheets × screws per sheet × (1 + waste)); boxes = ceil(screws ÷ 1000)
variables: sheets (count | count) = 18 | 18; perSheet (count | count) = 32 | 32; waste (% | %) = 5 | 5
assumptions: 32 screws per 4×8 sheet is a common wall hang; ceilings and 5/8 board often need more. | Boxes always round up to 1,000-count packaging. | Adhesive and nails are excluded.

name: Drywall tape
description: Joint-tape rolls from net board area using a stated linear-feet-per-square-foot rule of thumb.
formula: board area × tape per ft² × (1 + waste) ÷ roll length
variables: coverage (ft² | m²) = 450 | 41.806368; tapePerSquare (ft / ft² | m / m²) = 1.5 | 4.92125984252; rollLength (ft | m) = 500 | 152.4; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: 1.5 ft of tape per ft² of board matches the companion drywall room estimate. | Paper, mesh and corner bead are different SKUs. | A framing-plan joint takeoff can be lower than 1.5 ft/ft² — change the factor.

name: Blown-in insulation calculator
description: Minimum whole-bag count from net area and the exact product, application and R-value chart's minimum-bags-per-1,000-ft² rate; optional extra stays separate.
formula: Area × (1 + optional extra) ÷ 1,000 × minimum bags per 1,000 ft²
variables: length (ft | m) = 40 | 12.192; width (ft | m) = 30 | 9.144; bagsPerThousand (bags / 1,000 ft² | bags / 1,000 ft²) = 36.5 | 36.5; waste (% | %) = 0 | 0
assumptions: Minimum bags per 1,000 ft² must be copied from the exact product, application and R-value chart. | Manufacturer charts can specify both a minimum bag count and minimum installed or settled thickness; the finished job must satisfy both. | Area is converted to square feet internally so the chart rate stays in bags per 1,000 ft². | This tool does not convert a climate code or R-value target into a bag count by itself. | Optional extra defaults to zero and must not duplicate settlement already built into the chart; it is applied before whole-bag rounding.
sources: Greenfiber SANCTUARY coverage chart <https://www.greenfiber.com/en-ca/products/sanctuary> | SOPREMA cellulose calculator and settled-thickness note <https://www.soprema.ca/en/sopra-cellulose-calculator> | U.S. DOE: insulation types and coverage <https://bsesc.energy.gov/energy-basics/types-insulation>

name: Board and batten
description: Board count and batten count from wall width, the exposed board face and a batten at each joint including the ends.
formula: boards = ceil(width ÷ face) × ceil(height ÷ stock) × (1 + waste); battens use boards + 1
variables: length (ft | m) = 20 | 6.096; height (ft | m) = 8 | 2.4384; boardWidth (in | mm) = 9.25 | 234.95; battenWidth (in | mm) = 1.5 | 38.1; stockLength (ft | m) = 8 | 2.4384; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Board count is ceil(wall width ÷ board face) × pieces per column. | Battens equal boards + 1 so each joint and both ends get a strip. | Openings are shown as area only; they do not auto-delete a board. Raise waste for a punched wall. | This is not a structural siding design.

name: Downspout
description: Downspout count from eave length and spacing, plus the number of stock pieces for the drop to grade.
formula: outlets = floor(eave ÷ spacing) + 1; pieces = outlets × drop × (1 + waste) ÷ piece length
variables: length (ft | m) = 60 | 18.288; postSpacing (ft | m) = 30 | 9.144; downspoutLength (ft | m) = 10 | 3.048; pieceLength (ft | m) = 10 | 3.048; waste (% | %) = 5 | 5
assumptions: Outlets = floor(eave ÷ spacing) + 1 so both ends get a drop. | Waste applies to pipe length only, not the outlet count. | Elbows, offsets and splash blocks are extra. This is not a rainfall design.

name: Fascia
description: Fascia-board sticks from eave plus rake run, rounded to the stock length you will buy.
formula: (eave + rake) × (1 + waste) ÷ stock length
variables: length (ft | m) = 60 | 18.288; rakeLength (ft | m) = 40 | 12.192; stockLength (ft | m) = 16 | 4.8768; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Hip roofs may have eaves only. Enter 0 for rake when there is no gable fascia. | Sub-fascia and finish fascia are different lines if the job uses both. | Mitres live in the waste field.

name: Foam board
description: Rigid-foam sheet count from wall area after openings and the face of one panel.
formula: (L × H − openings) × (1 + waste) ÷ sheet coverage
variables: length (ft | m) = 40 | 12.192; height (ft | m) = 9 | 2.7432; doors (count | count) = 2 | 2; windows (count | count) = 6 | 6; doorArea (ft² | m²) = 21 | 1.95096384; windowArea (ft² | m²) = 15 | 1.3935456; sheetCoverage (ft² | m²) = 32 | 2.97289728; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: A 4×8 rigid-foam panel is 32 ft² of face. Thickness and R-value are a spec, not this count. | Openings are deducted before waste. | Tape, fasteners and cladding are excluded.

name: Gutter calculator
description: Gutter and downspout piece counts from eave length, stock piece length and downspout runs.
formula: Gutter pieces = ceil(run × (1 + waste) ÷ piece length)
variables: runLength (ft | m) = 40 | 12.192; pieceLength (ft | m) = 10 | 3.048; downspouts (count | count) = 2 | 2; downspoutLength (ft | m) = 10 | 3.048; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Gutter waste applies to the eave run before whole-piece rounding. | Each downspout is counted as a drop plus its footage; fittings, outlets and hangers are excluded. | Piece length must match the stock you will buy.

name: Insulation calculator
description: Batt or roll count from net coverage area, product coverage and a visible cutting allowance.
formula: Length × width × (1 + waste) ÷ package coverage
assumptions: Coverage must use the selected batt or roll package, not a generic R-value chart. | Waste is applied before whole-package rounding. | This tool does not select R-value, cavity depth or blown-in bag yield.
sources: U.S. DOE: insulation types and coverage <https://bsesc.energy.gov/energy-basics/types-insulation>

name: Siding calculator
description: Wall and gable siding area after openings, then squares and coverage units with a visible allowance.
formula: (wall length × height + gable triangles − openings) × (1 + waste) ÷ 100
variables: length (ft | m) = 40 | 12.192; height (ft | m) = 9 | 2.7432; doors (count | count) = 2 | 2; windows (count | count) = 6 | 6; doorArea (ft² | m²) = 21 | 1.95096384; windowArea (ft² | m²) = 15 | 1.3935456; gableWidth (ft | m) = 0 | 0; gableHeight (ft | m) = 0 | 0; gableCount (count | count) = 0 | 0; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: One square equals 100 ft² of coverage. | Door and window deductions are editable planning areas. | Each gable is treated as a triangle of ½ × width × height. | Starter, trim, corners and soffit are excluded. | Waste is applied before whole-square rounding.

name: Soffit
description: Soffit panel count from eave length, soffit width and the face of one panel.
formula: eave × soffit width × (1 + waste) ÷ (panel length × panel width)
variables: length (ft | m) = 60 | 18.288; soffitWidth (in | mm) = 16 | 406.4; pieceLength (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; pieceWidth (in | mm) = 12 | 304.8; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Area is eave length × soffit width. | Vented vs solid is a SKU, not this count. This is not an attic NFA design. | Returns and porch ceilings should be added as extra eave length.

name: Stucco calculator
description: Stucco bag count from net wall area, number of coats and the selected bag's coverage per coat.
formula: (wall length × height − openings) × coats × (1 + waste) ÷ bag coverage
variables: length (ft | m) = 40 | 12.192; height (ft | m) = 8 | 2.4384; doors (count | count) = 1 | 1; windows (count | count) = 2 | 2; doorArea (ft² | m²) = 21 | 1.95096384; windowArea (ft² | m²) = 15 | 1.3935456; coats (count | count) = 2 | 2; coverage (ft² | m²) = 50 | 4.645152; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Door and window deductions are editable planning areas. | Coverage is per bag per coat at the selected thickness. | Lath, paper, trim and colour-coat accessories are excluded. | Waste is applied before whole-bag rounding.
sources: Sakrete: stucco coverage calculators <https://www.sakrete.com/concrete-calculators/>

name: Vapor barrier
description: Poly roll count from floor or crawl area and the net coverage of one roll after the labelled lap.
formula: area × (1 + waste) ÷ roll coverage
variables: length (ft | m) = 40 | 12.192; width (ft | m) = 30 | 9.144; rollCoverage (ft² | m²) = 1000 | 92.90304; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Roll coverage must match the poly you will buy. | Perm rating and location in the assembly are a spec, not this count. | Tape, boots and mastic are excluded.

name: Vinyl siding
description: Vinyl-siding squares, starter pieces and J-channel from wall area after openings.
formula: (wall + gables − openings) × (1 + waste) ÷ 100; starter and J-channel ÷ stock length
variables: length (ft | m) = 40 | 12.192; height (ft | m) = 9 | 2.7432; doors (count | count) = 2 | 2; windows (count | count) = 6 | 6; doorArea (ft² | m²) = 21 | 1.95096384; windowArea (ft² | m²) = 15 | 1.3935456; gableWidth (ft | m) = 0 | 0; gableHeight (ft | m) = 0 | 0; gableCount (count | count) = 0 | 0; pieceLength (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: One square equals 100 ft² of coverage after waste. | Starter follows the eave length. J-channel uses 17 ft per door and 12 ft per window as planning perimeters. | House wrap, foam, soffit and corners are excluded.

name: House wrap
description: Weather-resistive-barrier roll count from wall perimeter, height, opening deductions and the net coverage of one roll.
formula: (perimeter × height − openings) × (1 + waste) ÷ roll coverage
variables: length (ft | m) = 140 | 42.672; height (ft | m) = 9 | 2.7432; doors (count | count) = 2 | 2; windows (count | count) = 8 | 8; doorArea (ft² | m²) = 21 | 1.95096384; windowArea (ft² | m²) = 15 | 1.3935456; rollCoverage (ft² | m²) = 900 | 83.612736; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Perimeter times height minus door and window openings. | Roll coverage must be the labelled net of the product you will buy. | Tape, caps and window flashing are excluded. This is not a drainage-plane design.

name: Aluminum fence
description: Aluminum panels, posts and rails from run length, section width and a measured gate opening.
formula: panels = ceil((run − gates × gate width) ÷ section × (1 + waste)); posts = panels + 1 + gates
variables: length (ft | m) = 80 | 24.384; height (ft | m) = 4 | 1.2192; sectionWidth (ft | m) = 6 | 1.8288; gates (count | count) = 1 | 1; gateWidth (ft | m) = 4 | 1.2192; railsPerSection (count | count) = 3 | 3; waste (% | %) = 5 | 5
assumptions: Gate width is the measured opening, not a hidden 4 ft stand-in. | Posts = panels + 1 + gates. Caps and concrete are companion lines. | Racking for slope is excluded.

name: Fence post caps
description: Post-cap count from the posts you will set, plus a visible spare allowance.
formula: caps = ceil(posts × (1 + spare))
variables: count (count | count) = 14 | 14; waste (% | %) = 5 | 5
assumptions: Count the posts you will set, including gate posts. | Pyramid, flat and solar caps are a SKU, not this number. | Concrete bags stay the post-hole tool.

name: Chain-link fence calculator
description: Chain-link fabric rolls, line posts, terminal posts and top-rail pieces from run length and spacing.
formula: posts = floor(length ÷ spacing) + 1; rolls = ceil(length × (1 + waste) ÷ roll length)
variables: length (ft | m) = 100 | 30.48; postSpacing (ft | m) = 10 | 3.048; terminalPosts (count | count) = 2 | 2; rollLength (ft | m) = 50 | 15.24; railLength (ft | m) = 10 | 3.048; waste (% | %) = 5 | 5
assumptions: Post count is floor(run ÷ spacing) + 1 so both ends are included. | Line posts are total posts minus the terminal, corner and gate posts you enter. | Fabric waste is applied; posts and top rail are counted from geometry without a second hidden allowance. | Mesh height, gauge, fittings, tension wire and gates are excluded.

name: Fence gate
description: Gate kits, gate posts and latch hardware from opening count and width. Not a fence-run takeoff.
formula: kits = gate count; posts = kits × 2; latch kits = ceil(kits × kits-per-gate × (1 + spare))
variables: gates (count | count) = 2 | 2; gateWidth (ft | m) = 4 | 1.2192; quantity (count | count) = 1 | 1; waste (% | %) = 0 | 0
assumptions: Each leaf is one kit. A double drive gate is two kits. | Two posts per leaf. Deduct them from the run takeoff if you already counted the full centreline. | Hinge schedule, closer size and code swing are excluded.

name: Privacy fence
description: Solid privacy boards and posts from run length, board face and spacing. Picket-gap wood fence is a different count.
formula: boards = ceil(length ÷ board face × (1 + waste)); posts = floor(length ÷ spacing) + 1
variables: length (ft | m) = 100 | 30.48; height (ft | m) = 6 | 1.8288; postSpacing (ft | m) = 8 | 2.4384; boardWidth (in | mm) = 5.5 | 139.7; railsPerSection (count | count) = 3 | 3; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Boards sit tight — there is no picket gap on this page. | Post count is floor(run ÷ spacing) + 1 so both ends are included. | Gates, dog-ears and lattice tops are extras.

name: Fence stain
description: Fence-stain gallons from run length, height, faces stained and labelled coverage.
formula: length × height × faces × coats × (1 + waste) ÷ coverage
variables: length (ft | m) = 100 | 30.48; height (ft | m) = 6 | 1.8288; sides (count | count) = 2 | 2; coats (count | count) = 2 | 2; coverage (ft² / US gal | m² / US gal) = 200 | 18.580608; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Area is run × height × faces. Posts and rails live in the waste field. | Coverage must use the selected stain label, not a deck-stain default. | Pickets, gates and privacy boards are companion counts, not this gallon line.

name: Fence calculator
description: Wood-fence posts, rails, pickets and post-hole concrete bags from run length and spacing.
formula: posts = floor(length ÷ spacing) + 1; pickets = ceil(length ÷ (picket width + gap) × (1 + waste))
variables: length (ft | m) = 100 | 30.48; postSpacing (ft | m) = 8 | 2.4384; railsPerSection (count | count) = 3 | 3; picketWidth (in | mm) = 5.5 | 139.7; picketGap (in | mm) = 0.5 | 12.7; bagsPerPost (bags / post | bags / post) = 2 | 2; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Post count is floor(run ÷ spacing) + 1 so both end posts are included. | Picket waste is applied; posts, rails and concrete bags are counted from geometry without a second hidden allowance. | Gates, corners and slope stepping are not automatic deductions. | Bag count uses the entered bags-per-post planning value, not a designed footing.

name: Carpet calculator
description: Carpet area in square feet or metres, square-yard equivalent, and optional whole-roll or cut conversion.
formula: area to order = L × W × (1 + waste); selected units = area to order ÷ stated coverage
assumptions: Area including allowance is the direct planning answer; the selected roll or cut conversion uses the net coverage you enter. | Waste is added before the square-yard and whole-unit conversions. | This does not optimise roll direction, seams, pattern repeat or joins between rooms; confirm those with the installer.
sources: MeasureSquare: flooring coverage and layout context <https://www.measuresquare.com/tools/flooring-calculator/> | Lowe's: carpet measurement calculator <https://www.lowes.com/n/calculators/carpet-measurement-calculator>

name: Flooring cost calculator
description: Preliminary flooring material cost from measured area, visible allowance and user-entered rate.
formula: L × W × (1 + waste) × stated material rate
variables: length (ft | m) = 18 | 5.4864; width (ft | m) = 14 | 4.2672; ratePerSquareFoot (USD / ft² | USD / m²) = 3.5 | 37.6736864585; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Material rate is an editable planning input and may be stale. | Labor, delivery, tax, underlayment, removal and site preparation are excluded. | Waste is applied before pricing only when the starting area excludes overage.
sources: Lowe's: flooring project cost is estimate-only <https://www.lowes.com/n/calculators/vinyl-flooring-calculator>

name: Tile grout calculator
description: Grout volume and bag count from tile size, joint width, joint depth and floor area.
formula: Area × joint width × joint depth × (L + W) ÷ (L × W) × (1 + waste) ÷ bag yield
variables: length (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; width (ft | m) = 10 | 3.048; tileLength (in | mm) = 12 | 304.8; tileWidth (in | mm) = 12 | 304.8; jointWidth (in | mm) = 0.375 | 9.525; jointDepth (in | mm) = 0.375 | 9.525; bagYield (ft³ / bag | ft³ / bag) = 0.09 | 0.09; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Grout volume uses tiled area × joint width × joint depth × (tile length + tile width) ÷ (tile length × tile width). | Bag yield is the user-entered product yield, not a generic coverage chart. | Thinset, spacers and sealer are excluded. | Waste is applied before whole-bag rounding.

name: Laminate flooring calculator
description: Laminate floor coverage and whole-carton quantity with stated waste.
formula: L × W × (1 + waste) ÷ stated coverage
assumptions: Coverage should use the selected manufacturer's product label or quoted net coverage. | Waste is added before whole-unit purchase rounding. | Complex layouts, seams or patterns can require a higher documented allowance.
sources: MeasureSquare: flooring types and measured coverage <https://www.measuresquare.com/tools/flooring-calculator/>

name: Flooring material
description: Floor area and purchase packages with a clear waste allowance.
formula: L × W × (1 + waste) ÷ stated coverage
assumptions: Coverage should use the selected manufacturer's product label or quoted net coverage. | Waste is added before whole-unit purchase rounding. | Complex layouts, seams or patterns can require a higher documented allowance.

name: Self-leveling underlayment
description: Self-leveling bags from floor area, pour depth and the bag yield printed on the sack.
formula: bags = ceil(L × W × depth × (1 + waste) ÷ bag yield)
variables: length (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; width (ft | m) = 10 | 3.048; depth (in | mm) = 0.125 | 3.175; bagYield (ft³ / bag | ft³ / bag) = 0.4 | 0.4; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Depth is the average pour. Low spots live in the waste field. | Bag yield must match the self-level sack, not a mortar bag. | Thinset and grout are companion tile tools.

name: Tile thinset calculator
description: Thinset or tile-mortar bag count from tiled area, selected trowel coverage and a visible mixing allowance.
formula: Length × width × (1 + waste) ÷ bag coverage
assumptions: Coverage must come from the selected thinset bag at the actual trowel notch. | Waste is applied before whole-bag rounding. | Grout, backer board, sealer and movement joints are excluded.

name: Tile calculator
description: Floor tile coverage and whole-package quantity with a visible cut allowance.
formula: L × W × (1 + waste) ÷ stated coverage
assumptions: Coverage should use the selected manufacturer's product label or quoted net coverage. | Waste is added before whole-unit purchase rounding. | Complex layouts, seams or patterns can require a higher documented allowance.
sources: Best Tile: tile quantity and allowance guidance <https://www.besttile.com/tile-calculator>

name: Flooring underlayment calculator
description: Underlayment coverage and whole-roll quantity with stated lap allowance.
formula: L × W × (1 + waste) ÷ stated coverage
assumptions: Coverage should use the selected manufacturer's product label or quoted net coverage. | Waste is added before whole-unit purchase rounding. | Complex layouts, seams or patterns can require a higher documented allowance.
sources: MeasureSquare: flooring coverage and layout context <https://www.measuresquare.com/tools/flooring-calculator/>

name: Vinyl flooring calculator
description: Vinyl flooring coverage and whole-package quantity with a visible allowance.
formula: L × W × (1 + waste) ÷ stated coverage
assumptions: Coverage should use the selected manufacturer's product label or quoted net coverage. | Waste is added before whole-unit purchase rounding. | Complex layouts, seams or patterns can require a higher documented allowance.
sources: Lowe's: vinyl flooring material-estimation guidance <https://www.lowes.com/n/calculators/vinyl-flooring-calculator>

name: Cement backer board
description: Cement-board sheet count from wet-area floor or wall coverage and the face of one sheet.
formula: area × (1 + waste) ÷ sheet coverage
variables: length (ft | m) = 10 | 3.048; width (ft | m) = 8 | 2.4384; sheetCoverage (ft² | m²) = 15 | 1.3935456; waste (% | %) = 15 | 15
assumptions: A 3×5 cement board is 15 ft² of face; a 4×8 is 32 ft². | 15% waste is a common wet-area cutting figure, not a layout guarantee. | Thinset, tape, screws and waterproofing are excluded. This is not a shower-pan design.

name: Epoxy floor
description: Whole gallons of floor epoxy from garage or shop area, coats and the labelled coverage.
formula: area × coats × (1 + waste) ÷ coverage per gallon
variables: length (ft | m) = 20 | 6.096; width (ft | m) = 20 | 6.096; coats (count | count) = 2 | 2; coveragePerGallon (ft² / US gal | m² / US gal) = 150 | 13.935456; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Coverage is one coat of the selected epoxy. Primer, flakes and topcoat are often separate kits. | Coving, cracks and texture sit in the waste field. | This is not a moisture-test or surface-prep spec.

name: Subfloor
description: Tongue-and-groove subfloor sheet count from floor area and the face of one panel.
formula: L × W × (1 + waste) ÷ sheet coverage
variables: length (ft | m) = 20 | 6.096; width (ft | m) = 16 | 4.8768; sheetCoverage (ft² | m²) = 32 | 2.97289728; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: A 4×8 T&G panel is 32 ft² of face. | Adhesive, fasteners and blocking are excluded. | Stair openings should be split out or absorbed in waste on a small floor.

name: Vinyl fence
description: Vinyl panels, posts and caps from run length, panel width and gate openings.
formula: panels = ceil((run − 4 ft × gates) ÷ panel width × (1 + waste)); posts = panels + 1 + gates
variables: length (ft | m) = 80 | 24.384; height (ft | m) = 6 | 1.8288; panelWidth (ft | m) = 8 | 2.4384; gates (count | count) = 1 | 1; waste (% | %) = 5 | 5
assumptions: Each gate is treated as a 4 ft opening and is not a panel. | Posts = panels + 1 + gates. Gate kits, rails and concrete are separate lines. | Panel width must match the system you are buying.

name: Deck board calculator
description: Deck-board count and linear footage from deck size, board width, gap and stock length.
formula: rows = ceil(deck width ÷ (board width + gap)); boards = ceil(rows × run × (1 + waste) ÷ stock length)
variables: length (ft | m) = 16 | 4.8768; width (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; boardWidth (in | mm) = 5.5 | 139.7; boardGap (in | mm) = 0.125 | 3.175; stockLength (ft | m) = 16 | 4.8768; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Boards are assumed to run the entered board-run length. | Row count uses actual face width plus the planned gap. | Waste is applied to linear footage before whole-stock rounding. | Joists, posts, picture-frame borders and hidden fasteners are excluded.

name: Stair calculator
description: Preliminary riser count, tread run and stringer length from total rise and target step dimensions.
formula: risers = round(total rise ÷ target riser); run = (risers − 1) × tread; stringer = √(rise² + run²)
variables: totalRise (in | mm) = 105 | 2667; targetRiser (in | mm) = 7.5 | 190.5; targetTread (in | mm) = 10 | 254
assumptions: Riser count is the nearest whole number that fits the total rise at the target riser. | Tread count is risers minus one for a floor-to-floor flight that ends on the upper floor. | Stringer length is the geometric hypotenuse before birdsmouth, nosing or stock-width adjustments. | 2R + T is a carpentry comfort check, not a code approval. | This tool does not determine headroom, guards, nosing or local stair rules.
sources: Fine Homebuilding: stair rise and run geometry <https://www.finehomebuilding.com/>

name: AC tonnage
description: Compare an entered cooling-load scenario in kW, BTU/h and refrigeration tons. Includes an editable area factor.
formula: kW = (floor area m² × entered W/m² + additional W) / 1000; tons = kW × 3412.141633 / 12000
variables: length (ft | m) = 16.4041994751 | 5; width (ft | m) = 16.4041994751 | 5; loadWattsPerM2 (W / m² | W / m²) = 150 | 150; extraWatts (W | W) = 0 | 0
assumptions: The area factor is an entered scenario, not a climate-based equipment recommendation. | No automatic solar, ceiling, glazing, humidity, ventilation or occupant correction is inferred. | A qualified designer must calculate local design loads and select equipment. This is not Manual J or an electrical power estimate.
sources: ACCA Manual J: detailed residential load calculation <https://www.acca.org/standards/technical-manuals/manual-j>

name: Waterproofing membrane
description: Membrane roll quantities with explicit side and end laps, layers, upstand area and cutting allowance.
formula: rolls = ceil((roof area + detail area) × layers × (1 + waste/100) / ((roll width − side lap) × (roll length − end lap)))
variables: length (ft | m) = 32.8083989501 | 10; width (ft | m) = 32.8083989501 | 10; upstandAreaM2 (m² | m²) = 0 | 0; rollWidthM (m | m) = 1 | 1; rollLengthM (m | m) = 10 | 10; sideLapMm (mm | mm) = 100 | 100; endLapMm (mm | mm) = 150 | 150; layers (count | count) = 1 | 1; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Each roll is modelled with one side lap and one end lap; unused boundary laps are not recovered. | The additional area includes measured upstands/details; cutting allowance is separate from lap loss. | Dimensions and overlaps must match the specified membrane. This is an area estimate, not a roll-layout or waterproofing design.
sources: SikaShield E50: example product overlap requirements <https://ind.sika.com/en/construction/waterproofing-systems/preformed-membrane/sikashield-e50-hdpesain15mm.html>

name: Cement and sand plaster
description: Wall plaster cement bags and dry sand volume from net wall area, thickness and an entered volume mix.
formula: net area × thickness × dry factor × (1 + waste/100); cement kg = dry volume / (1 + sand parts) × bulk density
variables: length (ft | m) = 32.8083989501 | 10; height (ft | m) = 32.8083989501 | 10; openingsArea (ft² | m²) = 0 | 0; thickness (in | mm) = 0.590551181102 | 15; sandParts (ratio | ratio) = 4 | 4; dryFactor (ratio | ratio) = 1.33 | 1.33; cementDensity (kg / m³ | kg / m³) = 1440 | 1440; bagKg (kg / bag | kg / bag) = 50 | 50; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: One cement part to the entered sand parts by loose volume. | Dry-volume factor and cement bulk density are user-adjustable estimating assumptions, not laboratory values. | Waste applies once to both ingredients, then cement bags round up; sand moisture and bulkage are not separately calculated. | Use the specified coats, thickness and plaster system; this quantity calculation does not approve a mix.
sources: ASTM C926: application of Portland cement-based plaster <https://www.astm.org/c0926-24.html>

name: Steel weight
description: Rebar mass per metre, per bar and for a stated bar count from nominal diameter and steel density.
formula: kg/m = π × (diameter mm / 1000)² / 4 × density; kg = kg/m × bar length × count × (1 + waste/100)
variables: barDiameterMm (mm | mm) = 12 | 12; barLengthM (m | m) = 12 | 12; count (count | count) = 10 | 10; steelDensity (kg / m³ | kg / m³) = 7850 | 7850; waste (% | %) = 0 | 0
assumptions: Circular nominal bar area times the entered steel density; ribs and manufacturing tolerances are not separately modelled. | Diameter is always mm and bar length is always m, as labelled. | This weighs your bar schedule; it does not design reinforcement or optimize bar cuts.
sources: Qatar Steel: product specifications and applicable standards <https://www.qatarsteel.com.qa/qatar-steel-main-products/product-specifications/>

name: Caulk and sealant
description: Cartridge count from joint run and the linear coverage printed for one tube at the bead you will gun.
formula: joint run × (1 + waste) ÷ coverage per tube
variables: length (ft | m) = 80 | 24.384; coveragePerTube (ft / tube | m / tube) = 50 | 15.24; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Coverage is linear feet (or metres) of YOUR bead, not a universal 10.1 oz yield. | Backer rod, color and chemistry are excluded. | Start-stop and a spare tube live in the waste field.

name: Construction contingency calculator
description: Set aside a visible contingency allowance for preliminary project planning.
formula: Estimate cost × (1 + contingency)
variables: estimateCost (USD | USD) = 10000 | 10000; contingencyPercent (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Contingency is a separately stated planning allowance. | This tool does not predict final cost or prescribe a contingency percentage. | Amounts are stored internally in USD and converted to the selected display currency.

name: Construction markup calculator
description: Convert direct cost and a stated markup into a transparent customer price.
formula: Direct cost × (1 + markup)
variables: directCost (USD | USD) = 1000 | 1000; markupPercent (% | %) = 15 | 15
assumptions: Markup is calculated on direct cost, not on customer price. | Discount, tax, overhead and contingency require their own explicit estimate components. | Amounts are stored internally in USD and converted to the selected display currency.

name: Construction tax calculator
description: Calculate tax as a separately stated percentage of a taxable amount.
formula: Taxable amount × (1 + tax rate)
variables: taxableAmount (USD | USD) = 1000 | 1000; taxRate (% | %) = 8.25 | 8.25
assumptions: Tax treatment must be independently verified for the jurisdiction and contract. | The calculator applies the entered rate only to the entered taxable amount. | Amounts are stored internally in USD and converted to the selected display currency.

name: Material waste calculator
description: Add a transparent waste allowance to any measured material quantity.
formula: Base quantity × (1 + waste)
variables: baseQuantity (units | units) = 100 | 100; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: The base quantity must use one explicit, consistent purchasing unit. | Waste is added before any supplier package or delivery rounding. | This tool does not choose a waste factor or a material unit.

name: Furnace BTU
description: Planning heating load from floor area, ceiling height and a stated BTU per square foot. Not Manual J.
formula: BTU/h = area × BTU per ft² × (ceiling height ÷ 8)
variables: length (ft | m) = 40 | 12.192; width (ft | m) = 30 | 9.144; height (ft | m) = 8 | 2.4384; btuPerSqFt (BTU / ft² | BTU / ft²) = 30 | 30
assumptions: Planning factor times area, scaled by ceiling height over 8 ft. | Not Manual J, not a furnace size, not a code approval. | 30 BTU/ft² is a mild-climate start. Replace it with the factor you were given.

name: CFM
description: Planning airflow from room volume and air changes per hour. Not a duct design or Manual D.
formula: CFM = length × width × height × ACH ÷ 60
variables: length (ft | m) = 20 | 6.096; width (ft | m) = 15 | 4.572; height (ft | m) = 8 | 2.4384; airChanges (ACH | ACH) = 6 | 6
assumptions: CFM = volume × ACH ÷ 60. | ACH is a planning input, not a ventilation-code path. | Not Manual D, not a duct size and not a fan curve.

name: Asphalt calculator
description: Compacted asphalt volume and tonnage from area, depth and a stated mix density.
formula: L × W × compacted depth × (1 + waste) × density ÷ 2000
variables: length (ft | m) = 50 | 15.24; width (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; depth (in | mm) = 3 | 76.2; asphaltDensity (lb / ft³ | lb / ft³) = 145 | 145; waste (% | %) = 5 | 5
assumptions: Thickness is compacted installed depth. | Density is an editable mix-design input; 145 lb/ft³ is a common hot-mix planning value, not a guaranteed supplier density. | Tonnage is rounded up to the next 0.1 ton after allowance. | Base, binder, tack coat and compaction testing are excluded.

name: Gravel calculator
description: Bulk gravel volume, estimated weight, and a visible delivery allowance.
formula: Area length × width × depth ÷ 27 × (1 + waste)
variables: length (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; width (ft | m) = 10 | 3.048; depth (in | mm) = 3 | 76.2; density (US tons / yd³ | US tons / yd³) = 1.35 | 1.35; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Gravel area is treated as rectangular using average width. | The entered density is a supplier-specific planning input in tons per cubic yard. | Bulk volume is rounded up to the next 0.1 yd³ after allowance.
sources: Engineering ToolBox: bulk density of common materials <https://www.engineeringtoolbox.com/density-materials-d_1652.html>

name: Mulch calculator
description: Landscape bed volume, bulk mulch order, and whole-bag equivalent.
formula: Bed length × width × depth ÷ 27 × (1 + waste)
assumptions: Landscape bed geometry is treated as rectangular using average width. | Mulch depth represents installed compressed depth. | Bulk order is rounded to the next 0.1 yd³ after allowance.

name: Paver calculator
description: Patio area, individual paver face coverage, and whole-paver order quantity.
formula: Patio area ÷ paver face area × (1 + waste)
variables: length (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; width (ft | m) = 10 | 3.048; paverLength (in | mm) = 8 | 203.2; paverWidth (in | mm) = 4 | 101.6; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: The patio is treated as a rectangle and pavers are treated as a single face size. | Waste is applied before whole-paver rounding. | Base material, bedding sand, edge restraint and jointing material are excluded.
sources: Omni Calculator: Paver calculator methodology <https://www.omnicalculator.com/construction/paver>

name: Sand calculator
description: Bulk sand volume and tonnage from area, installed depth, a visible compaction factor and supplier density.
formula: L × W × depth ÷ 27 × (1 + compaction) × (1 + waste)
variables: length (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; width (ft | m) = 10 | 3.048; depth (in | mm) = 3 | 76.2; compaction (% | %) = 15 | 15; density (US tons / yd³ | US tons / yd³) = 1.35 | 1.35; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Installed depth is the compacted finished thickness. | Compaction factor adds loose volume before waste and 0.1 yd³ rounding. | Density is an editable supplier input in tons per cubic yard. | Joint sand, geotextile and edge restraint are excluded.

name: Sod calculator
description: Lawn area, waste allowance, and whole-roll sod purchase quantity.
formula: Lawn area × (1 + waste) ÷ roll coverage
assumptions: Roll coverage must match the selected supplier product. | Waste is applied before whole-roll rounding. | Irregular lawn areas should be divided into simple measured sections before totaling.
sources: Cool Runnings: Sod calculator and roll-coverage guidance <https://www.coolrunningslandscaping.com/tools/sod-calculator/>

name: Soil calculator
description: Bulk soil volume with a visible depth allowance and purchase rounding.
formula: Bed length × width × depth ÷ 27 × (1 + waste)
assumptions: Landscape bed geometry is treated as rectangular using average width. | Soil depth represents finished installed depth. | Bulk order is rounded to the next 0.1 yd³ after allowance.

name: Baluster spacing
description: Baluster count and clear gap for a run between posts, using a maximum opening you can set. Default 4 in is the common sphere-rule planning figure, not a code stamp.
formula: n = ceil((run − max gap) ÷ (baluster width + max gap)); gap = (run − n × width) ÷ (n + 1)
variables: length (ft | m) = 8 | 2.4384; balusterWidth (in | mm) = 1.5 | 38.1; maxGap (in | mm) = 4 | 101.6
assumptions: Count is the smallest number of balusters that keeps every clear gap at or under the maximum. | Run is inside-to-inside between posts. A gap sits at each post. | The 4 in default is a common residential sphere-rule planning figure, not a code stamp. | Posts, rail height and commercial rules are excluded.

name: Crown molding
description: Stock-length sticks of crown from the full room perimeter, with extra waste for coped inside corners.
formula: 2 × (L + W) × (1 + waste) ÷ stock length
variables: length (ft | m) = 16 | 4.8768; width (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; stockLength (ft | m) = 16 | 4.8768; waste (% | %) = 15 | 15
assumptions: Crown uses the full ceiling perimeter. Doors are not deducted. | Waste is higher than baseboard because coped insides throw away more offcut. | Vaulted and rake walls need their own measured run.

name: Wheelchair ramp
description: Ramp run length and slope percent from total rise and a stated slope ratio. Planning geometry only — not an ADA approval.
formula: run = rise × slope ratio; slope % = 100 ÷ ratio
variables: totalRise (in | mm) = 24 | 609.6; slope (ratio | ratio) = 12 | 12; width (ft | m) = 3 | 0.9144
assumptions: Run = rise × slope ratio. A ratio of 12 is the common 1:12 planning slope (8.33%). | This is geometry for a sketch and a material takeoff, not an ADA or accessibility approval. | Landings, handrails, edge protection and rest platforms are excluded. | A long run may need a landing; split the rise and add landing area as its own line.

name: Shiplap
description: Shiplap board count from wall width, height and the exposed face after overlap, rounded to whole sticks of the stock length you buy.
formula: ceil(wall width ÷ exposed face) × ceil(height ÷ stock) × (1 + waste)
variables: length (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; height (ft | m) = 8 | 2.4384; doors (count | count) = 0 | 0; windows (count | count) = 0 | 0; doorArea (ft² | m²) = 20 | 1.8580608; windowArea (ft² | m²) = 15 | 1.3935456; boardWidth (in | mm) = 5.25 | 133.35; stockLength (ft | m) = 8 | 2.4384; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Count uses the exposed face after overlap, not the nominal lumber size. | Pieces per course are ceil(wall height ÷ stock length). | Door and window deductions affect the area line, not the board count. Raise waste when you cut around openings. | Corners and cap trim are excluded.

name: Deck stain
description: Whole gallons of deck stain from deck area, coats and the coverage printed on the can.
formula: area × coats × (1 + waste) ÷ coverage per gallon
variables: length (ft | m) = 16 | 4.8768; width (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; coats (count | count) = 2 | 2; coveragePerGallon (ft² / US gal | m² / US gal) = 250 | 23.22576; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Coverage is one coat on the labelled product. Transparent and solid stains are not interchangeable. | Rails, stairs and end grain sit in the waste field or on a second line. | This is not a coating spec or dry-time schedule.

name: Baseboard and trim
description: Stock-length sticks of baseboard from room perimeter after door deductions, with a visible cutting allowance.
formula: (perimeter − doors × door width) × (1 + waste) ÷ stock length
variables: length (ft | m) = 16 | 4.8768; width (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; doors (count | count) = 2 | 2; doorWidth (ft | m) = 3 | 0.9144; stockLength (ft | m) = 16 | 4.8768; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Rectangular rooms use 2 × (length + width). Measure odd rooms as separate runs. | Baseboard stops at door openings. Casing and shoe are excluded. | Waste covers coped corners and scarf joints, not a second room.

name: Wainscoting
description: Stock-length sticks of wainscot from room perimeter after door deductions, with the chair-rail height kept visible for area.
formula: (perimeter − doors × door width) × (1 + waste) ÷ stock length
variables: length (ft | m) = 16 | 4.8768; width (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; height (ft | m) = 3 | 0.9144; doors (count | count) = 2 | 2; doorWidth (ft | m) = 3 | 0.9144; stockLength (ft | m) = 8 | 2.4384; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Rectangular rooms use 2 × (length + width) minus door openings. | Height is the chair-rail height used for the area line, not a second stock. | Cap rail, base and panels can be different SKUs. This count is one stock length.

name: Asphalt sealer
description: Whole gallons of driveway sealer from area, coats and the labelled coverage per gallon.
formula: area × coats × (1 + waste) ÷ coverage per gallon
variables: length (ft | m) = 50 | 15.24; width (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; coats (count | count) = 1 | 1; coveragePerGallon (ft² / US gal | m² / US gal) = 80 | 7.4322432; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Coverage is one coat on the labelled sealer. New asphalt tonnage is a different calculator. | A 5-gal pail is five of these gallons after whole-gallon rounding. | Oil-spot primer and crack filler are excluded.

name: Cut and fill
description: Cut volume, fill volume and net import or export from pad length, width and depths. Not a grading design.
formula: cut = L × W × cut depth ÷ 27; fill = L × W × fill depth ÷ 27; net = cut − fill
variables: length (ft | m) = 50 | 15.24; width (ft | m) = 20 | 6.096; cutDepth (in | mm) = 6 | 152.4; fillDepth (in | mm) = 4 | 101.6; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: A rectangle with two average depths. Split wild sites into more than one pad. | Swell and shrinkage live in the waste field. | Not a grading, drainage or retaining design.

name: Dump truck loads
description: Whole dump-truck loads from a stated material volume and truck capacity.
formula: loads = ceil(volume × (1 + load factor) ÷ truck capacity)
assumptions: Volume and capacity must use the same unit — both loose or both bank. | Capacity is the box you hired, not a universal 10-yard truck. | Wait time and dump fees are estimate extras.

name: Landscape fabric
description: Weed-barrier roll count from bed area and the net coverage of one roll after overlap.
formula: area × (1 + waste) ÷ roll coverage
variables: length (ft | m) = 20 | 6.096; width (ft | m) = 8 | 2.4384; rollCoverage (ft² | m²) = 150 | 13.935456; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Roll coverage must match the fabric width and length you will buy. | Pins and the mulch or rock on top are excluded. | Cut slits at plants; that is what the waste field is for.

name: Fill dirt
description: Fill-dirt volume and tonnage from area and compacted depth, with swell sitting in the waste field.
formula: L × W × D ÷ 27 × (1 + waste)
variables: length (ft | m) = 20 | 6.096; width (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; depth (in | mm) = 12 | 304.8; density (US tons / yd³ | US tons / yd³) = 1.2 | 1.2; waste (% | %) = 20 | 20
assumptions: Depth is compacted thickness. Swell lives in the waste field. | Density is a pit planning input in tons per cubic yard. | Topsoil, export haul-off and engineered fill specs are excluded.

name: French drain
description: Drainage-stone volume, pipe length and wrap-fabric area from trench length, width, depth and pipe diameter.
formula: (L × W × D − pipe cylinder) × (1 + waste) ÷ 27
variables: length (ft | m) = 50 | 15.24; width (ft | m) = 1 | 0.3048; depth (in | mm) = 24 | 609.6; pipeDiameter (in | mm) = 4 | 101.6; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Stone volume is the trench prism minus the pipe cylinder. Waste applies to the stone. | Fabric area wraps the three buried faces: 2 × depth + width. | This is not a drainage design. Slope, outlets and stone gradation stay with you. | Sleeved pipe may not need the wrap-fabric line.

name: Gravel driveway
description: Driveway gravel volume and tonnage from length, width, compacted depth and supplier density.
formula: L × W × D ÷ 27 × (1 + waste)
variables: length (ft | m) = 50 | 15.24; width (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; depth (in | mm) = 4 | 101.6; density (US tons / yd³ | US tons / yd³) = 1.4 | 1.4; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Area is a rectangle using average width. | Depth is the compacted or installed thickness, not a loose dump. | Density is a supplier planning input in tons per cubic yard. | Fabric, edging and subgrade work are excluded.

name: Paver base
description: Crushed-stone base and bedding-sand volumes under a patio from area, base thickness and sand thickness.
formula: area × thickness ÷ 27 × (1 + waste) for base and for sand
variables: length (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; width (ft | m) = 10 | 3.048; depth (in | mm) = 4 | 101.6; sandDepth (in | mm) = 1 | 25.4; density (US tons / yd³ | US tons / yd³) = 1.4 | 1.4; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Patio is a rectangle using average width. | Base thickness is the compacted stone layer. Sand thickness is the bedding layer before compaction. | Pavers, edge restraint and geotextile are excluded.

name: Pool volume
description: US gallons of water in a rectangular or circular pool from plan size and average depth. Not a chemical dose.
formula: L × W × average depth × 7.48052 gal/ft³
variables: shape (choice | choice) = 0 | 0; length (ft | m) = 32 | 9.7536; width (ft | m) = 16 | 4.8768; diameter (ft | m) = 24 | 7.3152; avgDepth (ft | m) = 5 | 1.524
assumptions: Average depth is the mean of the shallow and deep ends, not the deep end only. | Rectangle uses waterline length × width. Circle uses waterline diameter. | 7.48052 US gallons per cubic foot. This is a fill number, not a sanitizer dose. | Freeform pools should be split into simple shapes and added.

name: Polymeric sand
description: Bag count of joint sand from patio area and the coverage printed on the polymeric-sand bag.
formula: patio area × (1 + waste) ÷ coverage per bag
variables: length (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; width (ft | m) = 10 | 3.048; coveragePerBag (ft² / bag | m² / bag) = 50 | 4.645152; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Coverage must match the bag you will buy. Joint width and paver size change it. | Waste covers the second sweep after watering. | Edge restraint and the pavers themselves are excluded.

name: Road base
description: Crusher-run or class II base volume and tonnage from driveway or pad area, compacted depth and supplier density.
formula: L × W × D ÷ 27 × (1 + waste)
variables: length (ft | m) = 50 | 15.24; width (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; depth (in | mm) = 6 | 152.4; density (US tons / yd³ | US tons / yd³) = 1.5 | 1.5; waste (% | %) = 15 | 15
assumptions: Depth is compacted crusher-run or class II. Compaction lives in the waste field. | Density is a quarry planning input. | The wearing course of gravel is a separate line.

name: River rock
description: Decorative river-rock volume and tonnage from bed area, installed depth and supplier density.
formula: L × W × D ÷ 27 × (1 + waste)
variables: length (ft | m) = 20 | 6.096; width (ft | m) = 8 | 2.4384; depth (in | mm) = 3 | 76.2; density (US tons / yd³ | US tons / yd³) = 1.35 | 1.35; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Area is a rectangle using average width. | Depth is the compacted or installed thickness, not a loose dump. | Density is a supplier planning input in tons per cubic yard. | Fabric, edging and subgrade work are excluded.

name: Grass seed
description: Pounds of seed from lawn area and the labelled rate per 1,000 square feet.
formula: area ÷ 1,000 × rate × (1 + waste)
variables: length (ft | m) = 50 | 15.24; width (ft | m) = 40 | 12.192; ratePerThousand (lb / 1,000 ft² | lb / 1,000 ft²) = 5 | 5; waste (% | %) = 5 | 5
assumptions: Rate is pounds per 1,000 ft² from the bag you will buy. | New lawn and overseed rates are not interchangeable. | Starter fertilizer, straw and sod are excluded.

name: Board foot calculator
description: Lumber board-foot quantity from stated thickness, width, length, piece count and allowance.
formula: Thickness (in) × width (in) × length (ft) × quantity ÷ 12 × (1 + waste)
variables: lumberThickness (in | mm) = 2 | 50.8; lumberWidth (in | mm) = 6 | 152.4; stockLength (ft | m) = 10 | 3.048; quantity (count | count) = 10 | 10; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Board-foot arithmetic uses the stated thickness and width pricing basis, not an assumed nominal or actual size. | Metric dimensions are converted to inches before the board-foot formula. | Waste is a transparent planning allowance and supplier tally rules can differ.
sources: Hardwood Industries: board-foot calculator <https://www.hardwoodind.com/bfcalc/>

name: Floor joist calculator
description: Preliminary joist count and total linear footage from framing run, span and stated spacing.
formula: (floor(framing width ÷ spacing) + 1) × (1 + waste)
variables: length (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; width (ft | m) = 20 | 6.096; joistSpacing (in | mm) = 16 | 406.4; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Count uses floor(framing width ÷ stated spacing) + 1. | This is a material-quantity calculation only; it does not select joist size, grade, span, hangers, blocking or structural connections. | Waste is applied to count before total linear footage is displayed.
sources: Autodesk: framing lumber takeoff guidance <https://www.autodesk.com/blogs/construction/framing-lumber-takeoff/>

name: Linear lumber calculator
description: Whole stock-board count from total linear run, selected stock length and visible allowance.
formula: Total run × (1 + waste) ÷ stock length → whole boards
variables: runLength (ft | m) = 120 | 36.576; stockLength (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: All runs are assumed to use the same stock material and stock length. | Waste is added before whole-board rounding. | Detailed cut lists and layout optimisation are excluded.
sources: Home Project Calculator: linear-lumber planning guidance <https://www.homeprojectcalculator.com/lumber-calculator/>

name: Rafter calculator
description: Preliminary paired-rafter count and rafter length from roof plan dimensions, pitch and spacing.
formula: Rafter length = √((width ÷ 2)² + ((width ÷ 2) × rise ÷ 12)²)
variables: length (ft | m) = 30 | 9.144; width (ft | m) = 20 | 6.096; rise (rise per 12 | rise per 12) = 6 | 6; rafterSpacing (in | mm) = 24 | 609.6; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Rafter length uses one half of a symmetrical roof's building width and the stated rise-per-12 pitch. | Overhang, ridge-board deductions, birdsmouth, valley/hip geometry and stock-length splices are excluded. | This tool is not a rafter-sizing or structural-design calculator.
sources: American Wood Council: span options resource <https://awc.org/resources/span-options-calculator-for-wood-joists-and-rafters/>

name: Plywood & sheet goods calculator
description: Whole sheet-goods quantity from rectangular coverage, selected sheet coverage and allowance.
formula: Coverage length × width × (1 + waste) ÷ sheet coverage
variables: length (ft | m) = 20 | 6.096; width (ft | m) = 16 | 4.8768; sheetCoverage (ft² | m²) = 32 | 2.97289728; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Coverage area is rectangular; complex geometry should be divided into measured sections. | Sheet coverage must match the selected product. | Waste is applied before whole-sheet rounding.
sources: Autodesk: sheathing takeoff guidance <https://www.autodesk.com/blogs/construction/framing-lumber-takeoff/>

name: Wall stud calculator
description: Preliminary wall-stud count from wall run, spacing, openings and a visible allowance.
formula: (floor(wall run ÷ spacing) + 1 + 2 per opening) × (1 + waste)
variables: length (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; studSpacing (in | mm) = 16 | 406.4; openings (count | count) = 1 | 1; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Baseline count is floor(wall run ÷ stated spacing) + 1 for end studs. | Each opening receives a visible preliminary two-stud allowance only; detailed headers, corners, intersections and cripples need a plan takeoff. | The three-plate run assumes one bottom and two top plates when applicable; confirm the framing design.
sources: Autodesk: framing lumber takeoff guidance <https://www.autodesk.com/blogs/construction/framing-lumber-takeoff/>

name: Brick calculator
description: Brick count and mortar-bag planning from wall area, opening deductions and nominal brick face size.
formula: (wall length × height − openings) ÷ (nominal face length × height) × (1 + waste)
variables: length (ft | m) = 20 | 6.096; height (ft | m) = 8 | 2.4384; brickLength (in | mm) = 8 | 203.2; brickHeight (in | mm) = 2.67 | 67.818; doors (count | count) = 1 | 1; windows (count | count) = 2 | 2; doorArea (ft² | m²) = 21 | 1.95096384; windowArea (ft² | m²) = 15 | 1.3935456; bricksPerMortarBag (bricks / bag | bricks / bag) = 140 | 140; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Nominal face dimensions include the mortar joint. | Door and window deductions are editable planning areas, not a substitute for measured openings. | Mortar bags use the entered yield and do not include core grout, lintels or reinforcement. | Waste is applied before whole-unit rounding.
sources: BIA: brick sizes and modular planning <https://www.gobrick.com/>

name: Concrete block calculator
description: CMU count and mortar-bag planning from wall area, opening deductions and nominal block face size.
formula: (wall length × height − openings) ÷ (nominal face length × height) × (1 + waste)
variables: length (ft | m) = 20 | 6.096; height (ft | m) = 8 | 2.4384; blockLength (in | mm) = 16 | 406.4; blockHeight (in | mm) = 8 | 203.2; doors (count | count) = 1 | 1; windows (count | count) = 0 | 0; doorArea (ft² | m²) = 21 | 1.95096384; windowArea (ft² | m²) = 15 | 1.3935456; blocksPerMortarBag (blocks / bag | blocks / bag) = 33 | 33; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Nominal face dimensions include the mortar joint. | Door and window deductions are editable planning areas, not a substitute for measured openings. | Mortar bags use the entered yield and do not include core grout, lintels or reinforcement. | Waste is applied before whole-unit rounding.
sources: NCMA: concrete masonry unit sizes <https://ncma.org/>

name: CMU grout fill
description: Grout volume and 80 lb bag equivalent to fill CMU cores from wall face, block module and grout per block.
formula: ceil(L ÷ block length) × ceil(H ÷ block height) × grout per block × (1 + waste)
variables: length (ft | m) = 20 | 6.096; height (ft | m) = 8 | 2.4384; blockLength (in | mm) = 16 | 406.4; blockHeight (in | mm) = 8 | 203.2; groutPerBlock (ft³ / block | ft³ / block) = 0.25 | 0.25; waste (% | %) = 5 | 5
assumptions: Block count is wall face divided by the nominal module, with no opening deduction. | Grout per block is the core volume of one fully grouted unit. Partial-height grout and bond beams are extra. | Ready-mix rounds to the next 0.25 yd³. 80 lb bags assume 0.60 ft³ yield.

name: Mortar bags
description: Type N/S mortar volume and bag count from net wall area using a published 5.5 ft³ per 100 ft² rule of thumb.
formula: mortar ft³ = area ÷ 100 × 5.5; bags = ceil(mortar × (1 + waste) ÷ bag yield)
variables: coverage (ft² | m²) = 160 | 14.8644864; bagSize (choice | choice) = 80 | 80; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: 5.5 ft³ per 100 ft² is a 3/8 in joint rule of thumb for modular brick and 8 in CMU bed joints. | Bag yield is 0.45 ft³ for 60 lb and 0.60 ft³ for 80 lb planning bags; confirm the product label. | This is not a mix design and does not select Type N versus Type S.

name: Retaining wall block
description: SRW and garden-block count from exposed face area and the selected block face.
formula: blocks = ceil(length × height ÷ (block length × block height) × (1 + waste))
variables: length (ft | m) = 24 | 7.3152; height (ft | m) = 4 | 1.2192; blockLength (in | mm) = 16 | 406.4; blockHeight (in | mm) = 8 | 203.2; waste (% | %) = 5 | 5
assumptions: Count uses exposed face only. Buried base course, caps, glue and geogrid are excluded. | Waste is applied before whole-block rounding. | This is not a structural, drainage or setback design.

name: Stone veneer
description: Manufactured-stone carton count from net face area and the coverage printed on the carton.
formula: cartons = ceil(area ÷ carton coverage × (1 + waste))
variables: coverage (ft² | m²) = 120 | 11.1483648; unitCoverage (ft² | m²) = 10 | 0.9290304; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Carton coverage must match the product you will buy. | Corners, sills and mortar are excluded. | This is not a structural veneer, tie or WRB design.

name: Ceiling paint calculator
description: Ceiling paint coverage, coats, allowance and whole-gallon purchase quantity.
formula: Ceiling length × ceiling width × coats × (1 + waste) ÷ stated coverage
variables: length (ft | m) = 16 | 4.8768; width (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; coats (count | count) = 2 | 2; coverage (ft² / US gal | m² / US gal) = 375 | 34.83864; waste (% | %) = 5 | 5
assumptions: Ceiling area uses finished length × finished width. | Coverage must use the selected ceiling-paint product label. | Waste is applied before whole-gallon purchase rounding.
sources: Benjamin Moore: paint calculator guidance <https://www.benjaminmoore.com/en-us/paint-calculator>

name: Paint cost calculator
description: Preliminary finish-paint material cost from whole gallons, a stated rate and visible allowance.
formula: Base quantity × (1 + allowance) × stated material rate
variables: gallons (US gal | US gal) = 3 | 3; ratePerGallon (USD / US gal | USD / US gal) = 48 | 48; waste (% | %) = 0 | 0
assumptions: Material rate is an editable planning input and may be stale. | Any allowance remains visible before material pricing. | Labor, delivery, tax, accessories and installation are separate estimate components.

name: Exterior paint
description: Exterior-paint gallons from wall length, height, openings, coats and labelled coverage. Interior rooms use the paint calculator.
formula: (wall length × height − openings) × coats × (1 + waste) ÷ coverage
variables: length (ft | m) = 40 | 12.192; height (ft | m) = 9 | 2.7432; doors (count | count) = 2 | 2; windows (count | count) = 6 | 6; doorArea (ft² | m²) = 21 | 1.95096384; windowArea (ft² | m²) = 15 | 1.3935456; coats (count | count) = 2 | 2; coverage (ft² / US gal | m² / US gal) = 350 | 32.516064; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: This is a straight elevation, not a room perimeter. | Measure gables separately as base × vertical height ÷ 2. On a separate takeoff, enter half the base as wall length, the gable height and measured openings; keep waste separate. | Trim enamel is the trim calculator.

name: Interior paint calculator
description: Room wall area, opening deductions, coats and rounded paint purchase quantity.
formula: (2 × (L + W) × H − door deductions − window deductions) × coats ÷ coverage
variables: length (ft | m) = 16 | 4.8768; width (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; height (ft | m) = 8 | 2.4384; doors (count | count) = 1 | 1; windows (count | count) = 1 | 1; doorArea (ft² | m²) = 20 | 1.8580608; windowArea (ft² | m²) = 15 | 1.3935456; coats (count | count) = 2 | 2; coverage (ft² / US gal | m² / US gal) = 375 | 34.83864
assumptions: Gross wall area uses 2 × (room length + room width) × ceiling height. | Door and window deductions are editable planning assumptions, not a substitute for measured openings. | Coverage must use the selected paint product label; the purchase quantity rounds up to whole gallons.
sources: Benjamin Moore: room, doors and windows paint inputs <https://www.benjaminmoore.com/en-us/paint-calculator> | Glidden: paint coverage guidance <https://www.glidden.com/paint-calculator>

name: Paint primer
description: Primer gallons from room walls, openings, coats and labelled primer coverage. Finish paint is a different tool.
formula: (2 × (L + W) × H − openings) × coats × (1 + waste) ÷ primer coverage
variables: length (ft | m) = 16 | 4.8768; width (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; height (ft | m) = 8 | 2.4384; doors (count | count) = 1 | 1; windows (count | count) = 1 | 1; doorArea (ft² | m²) = 20 | 1.8580608; windowArea (ft² | m²) = 15 | 1.3935456; coats (count | count) = 1 | 1; coverage (ft² / US gal | m² / US gal) = 300 | 27.870912; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Room walls use 2 × (length + width) × height. Ceiling primer is the ceiling tool at one coat. | Coverage must use the primer label, not the finish-paint can. | Finish paint stays the interior paint calculator.

name: Paint trim
description: Trim-paint gallons from linear footage, coats and labelled linear coverage per gallon.
formula: trim run × coats × (1 + waste) ÷ linear coverage per gallon
variables: length (ft | m) = 120 | 36.576; coats (count | count) = 2 | 2; coverage (ft / US gal | m / US gal) = 400 | 121.92; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Coverage is linear feet (or metres) per gallon at your cut width, not wall square footage. | Base, casing and crown can share a line when the enamel is the same SKU. | Wall and ceiling paint stay companion room takeoffs.

name: Wall paint calculator
description: Straight-wall paint coverage, coats, allowance and whole-gallon purchase quantity.
formula: Wall length × wall height × coats × (1 + waste) ÷ stated coverage
variables: length (ft | m) = 20 | 6.096; height (ft | m) = 8 | 2.4384; coats (count | count) = 2 | 2; coverage (ft² / US gal | m² / US gal) = 375 | 34.83864; waste (% | %) = 5 | 5
assumptions: Wall area uses finished length × finished height. | Coverage must use the selected paint product label. | Waste is applied before whole-gallon purchase rounding.
sources: Glidden: paint coverage guidance <https://www.glidden.com/paint-calculator>

name: Wallpaper
description: Single-roll count from room perimeter, ceiling height, opening deductions and the usable coverage printed on the roll.
formula: (2 × (L + W) × H − openings) × (1 + waste) ÷ roll coverage
variables: length (ft | m) = 16 | 4.8768; width (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; height (ft | m) = 8 | 2.4384; doors (count | count) = 1 | 1; windows (count | count) = 1 | 1; doorArea (ft² | m²) = 20 | 1.8580608; windowArea (ft² | m²) = 15 | 1.3935456; rollCoverage (ft² | m²) = 56 | 5.20257024; waste (% | %) = 15 | 15
assumptions: Gross wall area uses 2 × (length + width) × height. | Door and window deductions are editable planning assumptions. | Pattern match lives in the waste field. Label coverage is not usable coverage on a large repeat. | This is not a hanging spec or adhesive schedule.

name: Roofing cost calculator
description: Preliminary roofing material cost from stated area, allowance and user-entered local rate.
formula: Base roof area × (1 + waste) × stated material rate
variables: coverage (ft² | m²) = 2000 | 185.80608; ratePerSquareFoot (USD / ft² | USD / m²) = 4.5 | 48.4375968752; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Material rate is an editable planning input and may be stale. | Labor, delivery, tax, accessories and other direct costs are excluded. | Waste is applied before pricing only when the starting area excludes overage.
sources: Procore: roof-area and material-estimation guidance <https://www.procore.com/library/calculators/asphalt-shingle-calculator>

name: Drip edge
description: Drip-edge piece count from eave run plus rake run, divided by the stock length you will buy.
formula: (eave + rake) × (1 + waste) ÷ stock length
variables: length (ft | m) = 60 | 18.288; rakeLength (ft | m) = 40 | 12.192; pieceLength (ft | m) = 10 | 3.048; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Drip edge is eave plus rake metal. Valleys and wall flashing are a different calculator. | Laps live in the waste field. | Profile (C or D) is a spec, not this count.

name: Roof flashing calculator
description: Whole flashing-piece quantity from required linear coverage and a visible allowance.
formula: Required flashing run × (1 + waste) ÷ piece coverage
variables: runLength (ft | m) = 60 | 18.288; pieceCoverage (ft | m) = 10 | 3.048; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Flashing pieces use the entered net usable coverage after overlap. | Waste is applied before whole-piece rounding. | Different roof details can require different flashing types and takeoffs.
sources: Procore: roof-detail material-estimation context <https://www.procore.com/library/calculators/asphalt-shingle-calculator>

name: Hip roof
description: Hip-roof area, squares and hip run from footprint, pitch and overhang. Gable shingles stay the roofing calculator.
formula: (L + 2×overhang) × (W + 2×overhang) × √(1+(rise/12)²) × (1 + waste) ÷ 100
variables: length (ft | m) = 40 | 12.192; width (ft | m) = 30 | 9.144; rise (rise per 12 | rise per 12) = 6 | 6; overhang (ft | m) = 1 | 0.3048; waste (% | %) = 12 | 12
assumptions: Rectangle with four 45° hips. Wings and valleys are extra lengths. | Overhang is added to both plan dimensions before the pitch factor. | Ridge-cap bundles stay the ridge-cap calculator. Not a rafter design.

name: Ice and water shield
description: Self-adhered ice-and-water roll count from eave length, coverage up the roof and valley length.
formula: (eave + valley) × coverage up the roof × (1 + waste) ÷ roll coverage
variables: length (ft | m) = 60 | 18.288; coverageWidth (ft | m) = 3 | 0.9144; valleyLength (ft | m) = 24 | 7.3152; rollCoverage (ft² | m²) = 200 | 18.580608; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Eave run times coverage up the roof, plus valleys at the same width. | How far the membrane must run is a code and climate input, not a default to leave blind. | Field underlayment for the rest of the roof is a different calculator.

name: Metal roof calculator
description: Pitched roof area and whole fixed-panel quantity using net area per selected panel.
formula: L × W × √(1 + (rise ÷ 12)²) × (1 + waste) ÷ net coverage
variables: length (ft | m) = 30 | 9.144; width (ft | m) = 20 | 6.096; rise (rise per 12 | rise per 12) = 6 | 6; panelCoverage (ft² | m²) = 36 | 3.34450944; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
