assumptions: Roof surface is calculated from a rectangular horizontal footprint and rise-per-12 pitch. | Coverage must be the net area of one fixed-length panel after side laps, not panel width. | Cut-to-length and site-formed systems require a profile-specific supplier takeoff. | Waste is applied before whole-unit purchase rounding.
sources: Sheffield Metals: standing-seam coil-estimation context <https://sheffieldmetals.com/learning-center/video/metal-roof-install-material-estimation-video/>

name: Roof pitch calculator
description: Roof pitch multiplier and slope angle from rise per 12 units of run.
formula: Slope multiplier = √(1 + (rise ÷ 12)²)
variables: rise (rise per 12 | rise per 12) = 6 | 6
assumptions: Pitch is expressed as vertical rise per 12 units of horizontal run. | This tool converts geometry only and does not determine roof design. | Use the multiplier with a measured horizontal footprint for preliminary material area.
sources: Procore: asphalt-shingle pitch multiplier guidance <https://www.procore.com/library/calculators/asphalt-shingle-calculator>

name: Ridge cap calculator
description: Hip and ridge cap bundles from measured ridge and hip length plus the selected bundle's linear coverage.
formula: (ridge + hips) × (1 + waste) ÷ bundle coverage
variables: ridgeLength (ft | m) = 30 | 9.144; hipLength (ft | m) = 40 | 12.192; coverage (ft / bundle | m / bundle) = 20 | 6.096; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Coverage is the usable linear coverage of the selected hip-and-ridge bundle. | Waste is applied to combined ridge and hip length before whole-bundle rounding. | Starter, ridge vent, drip edge and field shingles are excluded.

name: Roof shingle calculator
description: Pitched roof area, squares, type-specific shingle bundles and underlayment rolls.
formula: Footprint × √(1 + (rise ÷ 12)²) ÷ 100 × bundles per square × (1 + waste)
variables: length (ft | m) = 30 | 9.144; width (ft | m) = 20 | 6.096; footprintArea (ft² | m²) = 0 | 0; pitchPreset (rise per 12 | rise per 12) = 6 | 6; rise (rise per 12 | rise per 12) = 6 | 6; bundlesPerSquare (count | count) = 3 | 3; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Pitch uses the selected rise per 12 units of horizontal run. | The direct footprint area, when greater than zero, replaces length × width; it must be a measured horizontal area. | Selected shingle type uses 3 bundles per square; verify manufacturer coverage and packaging. | Underlayment roll coverage is a 1,000 ft² planning assumption before required overlap.
sources: Procore: asphalt-shingle calculation guidance <https://www.procore.com/library/calculators/asphalt-shingle-calculator>

name: Roof sheathing
description: Plywood or OSB sheet count from roof footprint, pitch multiplier and sheet coverage.
formula: L × W × √(1 + (rise ÷ 12)²) × (1 + waste) ÷ sheet coverage
variables: length (ft | m) = 30 | 9.144; width (ft | m) = 20 | 6.096; rise (rise per 12 | rise per 12) = 6 | 6; sheetCoverage (ft² | m²) = 32 | 2.97289728; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Footprint is the horizontal rectangle. Pitch uses rise per 12 of run. | A 4×8 panel is 32 ft² of face. Thickness and span rating are a spec, not this count. | Hips, valleys and rakes need a higher waste than a simple gable.

name: Snow load
description: Planning snow load in pounds from roof area and a stated ground snow load. Not a PE stamp.
formula: load = length × width × ground snow load
variables: length (ft | m) = 40 | 12.192; width (ft | m) = 30 | 9.144; snowPsf (lb / ft² | lb / ft²) = 30 | 30
assumptions: Pounds = horizontal area × the stated ground snow load. | Not ASCE 7, not a drift analysis, not a PE stamp and not a rafter size. | Replace the psf with the map or spec value you were given.

name: Starter strip
description: Starter-shingle bundle count from total eave length and the linear coverage printed on the starter bundle.
formula: eave × (1 + waste) ÷ coverage per bundle
variables: length (ft | m) = 100 | 30.48; bundleCoverage (ft / bundle | m / bundle) = 105 | 32.004; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Coverage is linear feet per starter bundle, not a shingle square. | Add rake length into the eave field if the spec wants starter there too. | Ice-and-water and field shingles are different calculators.

name: Roofing underlayment calculator
description: Pitched roof area and whole underlayment-roll quantity using stated roll coverage.
formula: L × W × √(1 + (rise ÷ 12)²) × (1 + waste) ÷ net coverage
variables: length (ft | m) = 30 | 9.144; width (ft | m) = 20 | 6.096; rise (rise per 12 | rise per 12) = 6 | 6; rollCoverage (ft² | m²) = 432 | 40.13411328; waste (% | %) = 10 | 10
assumptions: Roof surface is calculated from a rectangular horizontal footprint and rise-per-12 pitch. | Use the selected underlayment product's net roll coverage after the laps required for that product, roof slope and installation method. | Leak barriers at eaves, valleys, rakes and penetrations are separate quantities unless the specified system says otherwise. | Waste is applied before whole-roll purchase rounding.
sources: GAF FeltBuster installation instructions — product- and slope-specific laps <https://www.gaf.com/en-us/document-library/documents/installation-instructions-%26-guides/installation_instructions__feltbuster.pdf>

name: Ridge vent
description: Ridge-vent piece count from ridge length and the coverage of one vent section. Not a ventilation design.
formula: ridge × (1 + waste) ÷ piece length
variables: length (ft | m) = 30 | 9.144; pieceLength (ft | m) = 4 | 1.2192; waste (% | %) = 5 | 5
assumptions: This is a piece count, not an attic NFA or 1/150 ventilation design. | Shingle ridge cap is a different calculator. | End caps may be in the kit; 5% waste is a planning stand-in.

name: Roofing waste calculator
description: Add a stated roofing waste allowance to an independently measured roof area.
formula: Base roof area × (1 + waste)
assumptions: Starting area must already be slope-adjusted roof area. | This tool adds allowance but does not select a waste factor. | Supplier package coverage is applied separately after this calculation.
sources: Omni Calculator: roof-shingle calculation methodology <https://www.omnicalculator.com/construction/roof-shingle>

name: 3-4-5 check square
description: Diagonal of a rectangle so a layout can be squared in the field. Planning geometry only.
formula: diagonal = √(A² + B²)
assumptions: Diagonal = √(A² + B²). A 12 and 9 layout is a 3-4-5 scaled by 3. | Both diagonals of a rectangle must match before you pour or frame. | Not a survey, property-line check or control network.

name: Acreage
description: Acres, square feet and hectares from a rectangular tract. Not a survey.
formula: length × width ÷ 43,560
assumptions: Rectangle only. Split odd tracts and add the acres. | 43,560 ft² per acre. This is not a boundary survey. | Deed, GIS and tape acres can disagree — hire a survey when the line matters.

name: Area & volume calculator
description: Rectangle, circle and triangle geometry with area, perimeter and simple-prism volume displayed in multiple units.
formula: Area = L × W; Volume = L × W × depth
variables: shape (choice | choice) = 1 | 1; length (ft | m) = 12 | 3.6576; width (ft | m) = 10 | 3.048; height (ft | m) = 4 | 1.2192
assumptions: Geometry is treated as a simple rectangle using the displayed dimensions. | Extrusion depth creates a simple-prism volume only; it is not appropriate for tapered or irregular solids. | This utility does not apply a waste factor.

name: Grade and slope
description: Slope percent, ratio and angle from rise and run. Planning geometry only — not a drainage design.
formula: slope % = rise ÷ run × 100
variables: length (ft | m) = 50 | 15.24; gradeRise (ft | m) = 2 | 0.6096
assumptions: Percent = rise ÷ run × 100. Ratio is run per 1 of rise. | This is a triangle, not a drainage, ramp or driveway design. | Use the wheelchair-ramp calculator when you need run from a stated 1:12.

name: Length unit converter
description: Transparent source-to-target length conversion with side-by-side feet and metres equivalents.
formula: Source value × source-unit-to-feet factor ÷ target-unit-to-feet factor
variables: conversionValue (selected unit | selected unit) = 10 | 10; fromUnit (choice | choice) = 1 | 1; toUnit (choice | choice) = 2 | 2
assumptions: This tool converts linear length only. | All conversions pass through feet as the canonical internal unit. | Use the unit stated by the drawing, product label or survey source; do not mix length with area or volume units.

name: Pipe volume
description: Pipe gallons and cubic feet from inside diameter and length. Not a flow or plumbing-code design.
formula: gallons = π × (ID ÷ 2)² × length × 7.48052
variables: pipeDiameter (in | mm) = 4 | 101.6; length (ft | m) = 40 | 12.192
assumptions: Inside diameter, not the nominal trade size when they differ. | 7.48052 US gallons per cubic foot. Not a flow, friction or plumbing-code design. | Length is the pipe, not the trench.

name: Trench volume calculator
description: Geometric trench volume with an optional project-specific loose-volume or over-excavation factor and stated truck capacity.
formula: Length × width × depth ÷ 27 × (1 + verified volume factor) → adjusted volume
variables: length (ft | m) = 50 | 15.24; width (ft | m) = 2 | 0.6096; depth (in | mm) = 36 | 914.4; truckVolume (yd³ / truck | yd³ / truck) = 10 | 10; waste (% | %) = 0 | 0
assumptions: The trench is treated as an in-situ rectangular prism using average width and depth. | The factor is user-supplied; 0 means no loose-volume or over-excavation adjustment has been verified. | Planning truck loads use the entered usable truck volume and round up to whole loads; confirm material factor and load limits before hauling. | This tool does not design shoring, sloping or utility clearance.
sources: FHWA: earthwork volume and project-specific shrink/swell factors <https://highways.dot.gov/federal-lands/pddm/dpg/earthwork-design> | NIST SP 811: SI units and volume <https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/Legacy/SP/nistspecialpublication811e2008.pdf> | Texas DWC: trench safety (U.S. jurisdiction example) <https://www.tdi.texas.gov/pubs/videoresourcessp/spwpexcav.pdf>
